messages:
Auditor_Lina: Hi team — request for ISO/SOC2 evidence for the privilege elevation used during vuln triage on 2024-08-04 (INC-20240804-09). Need: RBAC delta, STS/AssumeRole traces, KMS Decrypt/GenerateDataKey events, approver proof, exact queries used to collect artifacts, SHA256 hashes, and a 2-sentence control mapping. Chain-of-custody must be explicit.

nate-sec: Acknowledged. We'll produce an isolated evidence bundle and include a manifest with the fields you listed. Which key ID is in scope?

Auditor_Lina: Key: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/pp11-qq22. Map to SOC2 CC6, ISO A.9.2/A.12.4. Include fallback procedure if KMS was unreachable.

rachel-oncall: Elevation was performed by runbook-service v4 as part of triage ticket TR-8899, approved by product-security (approver: prod-sec@redwood). TTL was 30m. I'll snapshot the runbook transaction and include the PR link.

ollie-sre: KMS events are in CloudTrail and forwarded to Splunk. I'll pull DECRYPT and GenerateDataKey calls for the key and cross-reference the CloudTrail eventIDs with STS AssumeRole events. Note: runbook creates an ephemeral session so you'll see sts:AssumeRole -> Decrypt under same session.

nate-sec: DB export plan: extract role_bindings rows where ticket='TR-8899' and audit_log entries for the grant. Command used: ```PGHOST=auth-db psql -c "COPY (SELECT * FROM role_bindings WHERE ticket='TR-8899') TO STDOUT WITH CSV" > rbac_TR-8899.csv```

ollie-sre: Splunk query used: ```index=cloudtrail eventName IN (Decrypt,GenerateDataKey) resources="pp11-qq22" userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName="runbook-service" | table _time, eventID, eventName, userIdentity, resources, requestParameters``` Returned 4 events in window.

rachel-oncall: Uploaded RBAC snapshot to internal snapshot store: https://internal.redwood/snapshots/TR-8899/rbac-snapshot-6301234575.csv (auditor access only).

export-bot: Evidence export job complete: s3://redwood-audit-exports/TR-8899/evidence-6301234580.tar.gz (expires 7d). Manifest URL: https://internal.redwood/manifest/6301234580. Preliminary SHA256: 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08 (full file will contain per-artifact SHA256s).

Auditor_Lina: Manifest must include: artifact_name, sha256, created_by, approver, control_map (comma-separated), event_ids (RBAC, STS, KMS), reproduction_queries, chain_of_custody (exporter, checksum_actor, storage_location). Also please redact external IPs.

nate-sec: Will do. Chain-of-custody: exported by rachel-oncall, checksum computed by export-bot, uploaded to S3 with auditors@redwood ACL. We'll include an HMAC-signed manifest entry in addition to SHA256s for extra integrity.

ollie-sre: Note for auditors: a telemetry worker pod also calls Decrypt to fetch runtime certs; we correlated via sessionToken and added a manifest note explaining the multi-principal appearance.

Auditor_Lina: Good — include that explanation in the manifest notes. Also attach a short narrative tying the RBAC change to the triage decision and fallback if KMS had been unavailable.

rachel-oncall: Draft narrative: "During INC-2024-08-04 we identified an exploitable dependency. Runbook-service required temporary elevated write access to patch the dependency and rotate secrets. The elevation was approved by product-security under TR-8899 with a 30-minute TTL. KMS decrypts were used to retrieve secret material; if KMS had been unavailable the runbook would have executed a documented read-only remediation and escalated to manual emergency procedures per the crypto-key fallback protocol."

nate-sec: Manifest snippet (uploaded): {"artifact":"evidence-6301234580.tar.gz","sha256":"9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08","created_by":"rachel-oncall","approver":"prod-sec","notes":"IPs redacted; multi-principal session explained; HMAC-signed"} (full manifest at manifest URL).

export-bot: Auditor access granted to group auditors@redwood for 168 hours. Pre-signed download link emailed to Auditor_Lina.

Auditor_Lina: Received package and manifest. Two last asks: 1) include the exact AWS CLI CloudTrail filter you used, 2) include the STS AssumeRole eventIDs so we can verify session chaining.

ollie-sre: AWS CLI CloudTrail example: ```aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2024-08-04T14:00:00Z --end-time 2024-08-04T15:00:00Z --query 'Events[?Resources[?ResourceName==`pp11-qq22`]]'``` STS eventIDs included in manifest: sts-evt-abc123, sts-evt-def456. KMS eventIDs: kms-evt-xyz789, kms-evt-uvw000. RBAC export event id: rbac-evt-rrt111.

nate-sec: Also included reproduction commands for DB export and exact Splunk query text in the manifest for reproducibility.

Auditor_Lina: Excellent. This satisfies the evidence request. I'll tag as accepted in the audit tracker unless I find issues during review. :thumbsup:

rachel-oncall: Filing a short post-incident note linking the incident, the evidence bundle, and the ISO control pack.

nate-sec: Closing Jira SEC-1529 and adding manifest and auditor confirmation.

export-bot: Ticket SEC-1529 status changed to Resolved by nate-sec at 2024-08-05T10:12:00Z.
